sections.history: Thirukkannamangai lies about six kilometres from Tiruvarur on the road to Kumbakonam. It is one of the 108 Divya Desams, the abodes of Vishnu sung by the Alvars in the Nalayira Divya Prabandham, and belongs to Chola Nadu, where Thirumangai Alvar hymned the Lord. The temple is believed to have been begun by the Medieval Cholas in the late ninth century, and three inscriptions of the Chola period are recorded here. The Thanjavur Nayaks of the seventeenth century are remembered for later additions and renovation. It is counted among the Pancha Krishnaranya Kshetrams, the five sacred groves of Krishna.
sections.architecture: A five-tiered rajagopuram opens the temple, and the sanctum is crowned by the Utpala Vimanam. The sacred tank is the Darshana Pushkarini, described as one of the largest temple tanks in the state. The presiding Lord is known as Perumpurakkadal, the great ocean outside, while the festival image bears the name Bhaktavatsalan, with Abhishekavalli as the festival image of the Goddess, who is honoured as Kannamangai Nayagi in her own shrine.
sections.legends: Tradition holds that Lakshmi was wedded to Vishnu at this place. The devas who witnessed the wedding, the sthala purana tells, took the form of bees and built a hive beside the Thayar shrine, on its northern side, so that they might stay and worship every day. The bees are said never to harm devotees, who may see the hive near the Goddess's shrine.
sections.festivals: The Brahmotsavam is held in the month of Chithirai, April–May, beginning ten days after Chitra Pournami and including a chariot festival. Vaikunta Ekadashi is kept with devotion, and the temple follows six daily rituals and three yearly festivals in the Vaishnava tradition.
sections.experience: A peaceful village Divya Desam within easy reach of Tiruvarur, rewarding for pilgrims who follow Thirumangai Alvar's hymns across the delta. Walk beside the broad Darshana Pushkarini, then look for the hive near the Thayar shrine. The Chithirai Brahmotsavam is the most festive time; other days are calm.

visit.timings: Open daily with morning and evening darshan sessions and a midday closure; festival days are busiest. Confirm current timings before visiting.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional dress is expected — shoulders and knees covered; footwear removed before entering. Follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.photography: Photography is restricted in and around the sanctum; follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.gettingThere: The temple is about six kilometres from Tiruvarur on the Tiruvarur–Kumbakonam road in Tamil Nadu. Tiruvarur is the nearest town and railhead, and Tiruchirappalli is the nearest major airport. Reach it by road from Tiruvarur, and confirm local directions on arrival.
